findings.observation: The refreshed figure is visibly a gold feline cub: two pointed ears with pink inner accents, large pale eye field and dark pupil/green iris, cream cheek and short muzzle, plus darker shoulder/body banding. These are coordinated face and body changes rather than palette-only changes.

Standing pose has a shorter cream muzzle and upright feline ears. The visible side eye is larger and clearer than the previous narrow dark eye. Foot placements and forward wrist remain source-aligned in the comparison; original forward snout silhouette is intentionally trimmed only here.

The large open mouth retains the source forward reach while the enlarged eye, ear accents and cream cheek preserve feline identity. It is reasonable for an extreme open-mouth pose to expose a longer jaw; do not force standing short-muzzle geometry onto this interaction endpoint.

Prone pose keeps the closed-eyelid variant, cream cheek, paired ears and gold/dark striping. Forward paws, lower body and rear extension retain the source arrangement. The upper rear projection remains source structure, not evidence of a newly articulated ear or wing.

Technical support changes are respectively 8 removed/13 added, 2 removed/4 added, and 3 removed/12 added. In the actual comparison these concentrate around the approved head/cheek/ear treatment and small internal contour repair. Same native bounds alone is not treated as proof of joint or endpoint equivalence.

nonBlockingLimitations: Native pixels are small: green iris and pink inner ear are supporting accents; silhouette, large eye and cream muzzle must remain primary identifiers.
Only three source poses were reviewed. The remaining motion masters, wrist ornament continuity and tail/ear occlusion still need per-pose inspection.
This direction pass does not approve complete animation, normal-game default replacement, five phone viewports, physical device testing or shipping.
reviewMethod: Actually viewed identity-comparison.png and all three source/authored rows in source-comparison.png at native and enlarged scales; read setting rules and technical support changes. The decision is visual and bounded, not inferred from test PASS.
